title: Review of c08's NRCH chemostat finding: on seed 4 the chemostat again stabilizes swimmers against the u=0 twin (16 vs 4 persistent tracks, 59 vs 12 BL), but no regular crystal forms by t=6000
summary: Fresh labkit runs of the finding's world.py (its defaults are the K5 arm: u=1.5e-3, phi0=phi_t=-0.4) and of the matched u=0 twin on seed 4 (192^2, T=6000, frames every 25 t, K=40). Chemostat: 16 persistent tracks (>= 50% of the run), longest 219 frames (5475 t), 25 tracks moving >= 1 BL, max 59.0 BL, 35 splits / 4 persistent (generation 1) / 17 merges. u=0 twin: 4 persistent tracks, longest 148 frames, max 12.0 BL, 55 splits / 0 persistent / 64 merges. The stabilization the finding reports replicates. The picture differs from K5 seed 0, though: on seed 4 the swimmers stay a polar flock of mixed round and rod-shaped bodies and do not lock into an evenly spaced lattice of identical crescents by t=6000 (k5_s4/sheet.png); and on seed 0 (the claim's K5 sheet) the 'crystal' fills the domain as a drifting hexagonal spot lattice, nearer a travelling pattern than free swimmers. Division stays absent (4 persistent splits, generation 1).

observations.S: k5_s4/sheet.png t=0: uniform state plus noise; spots by t=250
observations.I: k5_s4/FACTS.md: 16 persistent tracks, longest 5475 t, against 4 in u0_s4
observations.M: k5_s4/FACTS.md: 25 tracks >= 1 BL, max 59.0 BL; u0_s4: max 12.0 BL; polar flock on k5_s4/sheet.png t=1300-6000

seeds_run.result: pass for stabilization; no crystal lock by t=6000

controls_run.I: u0_s4/ (u=0, same seed, grid and duration)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. 'Traveling crystal of identical swimmers' is seed- or time-dependent: seed 4 shows mixed rods and round bodies with no lattice lock by t=6000. Where the lattice forms it fills the domain, so the bodies are spots of a travelling pattern as much as free individuals; body lengths then measure pattern drift. Division absent as stated.
